sentences.text: The claimants have filed this appeal for enhancement of compensation and the Insurer has challenged the impugned judgment both on the quantum as well as liability to pay the compensation.
2. Both the matters are slated for hearing on admission and with the consent on both the sides, it is taken up for final disposal.

3. It is the case of the claimants that on 26.03.2019 at about 4.30 p.m., the deceased Abdul Raheem Kamthan was going on a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-32/EA-1258 on Humnabad Ring Road from Kapnoor to Gunj.
On Humnabad Ring Road, he stopped his vehicle at traffic signal.

At that time, driver of the tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-33/A-2451 drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said motor cycle of NC: 2023:KHC-K:5964-DB the deceased,
because of the impact, deceased sustained grievous injuries.

He was shifted to Kamreddy Hospital,
Kalaburagi wherein he was admitted as an inpatient for aobut 14 days.
Thereafter, he was shifted to Narmada Hospital, Solhapur for higher treatment.
Unfortunately, he succumbed to the injuries on 31.05.2019 while undergoing treatment.
The claimants had spent more than Rs.15 Lakhs towards the treatment.
4. It was the further case of the claimants that claimant No.1 is wife and claimant Nos.2 to 6 are children of the deceased.
They were all depending upon the earning of the deceased.
With these reasons, they prayed to award compensation of Rs.34,70,000/-.
5. Respondent No.1 was the owner and Respondent No.2 was the Insurer of the offended tipper lorry.
In the Written Statement, both of them have denied contents of the claim petition and they also submitted that the compensation claimed is exorbitant.

The owner of the vehicle has submitted that the vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2 and Insurer is liable to pay the NC:
2023:KHC-K:5964-DB compensation.
The Insurer has contended that owner of the vehicle had violated terms and conditions of the policy of the insurance.
Therefore, it was not liable to pay the compensation.
It has also contended that the driver of the tipper lorry has no valid and effective license to drive the vehicle.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition against the Insurer.
6. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues.
7. The claimants examined PW-1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P28.
Both the respondents have not lead evidence.

9. We have heard the arguments.
10. The learned Advocate for the Insurer has submitted that income taken by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
There is no legally acceptable evidence to prove the income.
The driver of the tipper lorry had no valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle.
Even though contention was taken by the Insurer, the Tribunal has not assessed the same and fastened the liability on RespondentNo.2/Insurer.
Therefore, prayed to set aside the said judgment.
11. The learned advocate for claimants submit that the Tribunal has taken income on the lower side.
The amount of compensation awarded on the other heads are much less.
The Respondent/Insurer has not lead any evidence to prove its contention that the driver of the tipper lorry had no valid license to drive the vehicle.
Moreover, the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5964-DB Investigating Officer had not charge-sheeted the driver of the tipper lorry for the said offence.

The Respondent No.2 has not issued any notice to the owner of the vehicle requesting to provide copy of the driving license or issue a notice to the driver of the vehicle, to produce the driving license.

Without any such evidence,
it has disowned its liability to pay the compensation.
Therefore, prayed to reject the appeal filed by the Insurer.
12. The submission of the learned advocate for the claimants as stated above, is tenable.

The Insurer though denied that driver of the tipper lorry had valid and effective driving license, but has not taken any steps to secure information from owner of the said vehicle or driver of the said vehicle.

It Kausar Begum And Ors vs Himmatlal G. Chavan And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103771726/
6 has not examined any witnesses to prove the said contention.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The burden is on Respondent No.2 to show that driver of the said tipper lorry had no license to drive the vehicle since it is an assertive contention of Respondent No.2.
Without any evidence, it wants to disown its liability, which is not permissible.
As rightly submitted by the learned advocate for the claimants, the driver of the lorry was not charge-sheeted for driving the vehicle without valid license.
What is the basis for the Insurer to contend that the driver of the lorry had no license to drive the notice, is not disclosed in any part of the evidence or pleadings.
Therefore, the said submission is not acceptable.
Respondent/Insurer had utterly failed to prove that driver of the tipper lorry had no valid or effective valid driving license.

Moreover, for any reason, the Insurer has found that driver of the tipper lorry had no valid license, then, it is the duty of the Insurer to pay the compensation to the claimants and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in an appropriate proceeding, if it is able to establish its case.
On that count, it cannot disown its liability.
14. Both the claimants and Insurer have contended that amount of income taken by the Tribunal is not proper.
The claimants have contended that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month as salary by working as a Manager in Lucky Motors.
There are no records to prove the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5964-DB said contention.
Therefore, the Tribunal has taken notional income of the deceased as Rs.13,250/-.
The said finding of the Tribunal is proper and does not call for any interference.

While settlement of the dispute in Lok-Adalath, in respect of the motor vehicle compensation case, as per the Guidelines prescribed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for an accident taken place during the year 2018, notional income of the victim of an accident is taken as Rs.13,250/-.
The same is taken by the Tribunal.
It does not call for any interference.
15. The learned Advocate for the Insurer has also tried to contend that age of the deceased was 40 years.
Therefore, adding 40% of income towards future prospects is not proper and it ought to be taken as 25%.
The said submission is also not acceptable.
The Tribunal has noted age of the deceased as 39 years on the basis of date of birth mentioned in the SSLC Marks-card as 05.09.1980.

Therefore, as per the law laid down in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5964-DB OTHERS1, claimants are entitled for addition of 40% of income towards future prospects.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5964-DB OTHERS1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no error in the said findings of the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded Kausar Begum And Ors vs Himmatlal G. Chavan And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103771726/
7 medical expenses on the basis of actual receipts produced by the claimants.

entities.text: Kausar Begum And Ors vs Himmatlal G. Chavan And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the cross-examination of PW-1, the insurer has not brought out anything to show that the said medical bills were created or concocted.
Therefore, the said finding is also proper.
The Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable amount of compensation on all other heads and it does not call for any interference by this Court.

16. For the aforesaid reasons, we pass the following:
ORDER
Both the appeals, M.F.A.No.201446 of 2022 and M.F.A.No.201032 of 2022 are dismissed.
The impugned judgment and award passed by the 1st Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi in M.V.C.No.835/2019 dated 17.11.2021 is confirmed.
